nesnd_south_succession_board_reason: Whose realm is the South: the Zhu emperor's, or the one the Zheng family carved out? Nanjing still holds the Ming succession; the Southern Administration in Hangzhou commands the troops and revenue that drive reform. While the Western provinces and Hangzhou stood together against the North, the question of sovereign and minister could wait. Now reform has reached deep into the provinces, and neither side can dodge the question of who governs.\n\nHuguang's academies and the Xiangfan garrisons keep the Zhu calendar; Sichuan's republicans are still arguing over Hangzhou's reforms. The governors of the Southern Seas and the lords of Japan are reckoning up how much land, money and manpower a change of dynasty will demand of them.
nesnd_board_choose_neutral_desc: Let the Ming court and Hangzhou quarrel as they please. We will look after our own trade and defence.
nesnd_board_choose_autonomy_desc: While the court fights over the succession, take our taxes, appointments and defence back into our own hands. Make that plain to Ming and Wu alike.
nesnd_ming_court.3.d: The ministers who followed the sovereign have reached the refuge, and the local officials are busy settling the court in. The garrison here must still raise supplies and draft men, the administrative commission must still govern the counties, and now there is a travelling court to feed as well. Ming loyalists finally have a sovereign to serve; and the host province has become the first to break openly with Hangzhou.\n\nEnvoys from the provinces and overseas states are still on the road. The claims once argued in the Assembly of Rites and the cabinet will be settled by soldiers from now on.
nesnd_ming_court.9.d: Neither Huguang nor Sichuan has a government able to receive the sovereign, so the court must stay in Nanjing. Ming loyalist ministers are canvassing the provinces with one hand and parrying Hangzhou, which holds the troops and the money, with the other. The Zheng bid for the throne is already on the table.
nesnd_ming_court.10.d: Those who oppose the new dynasty have not yet formed an alliance able to take up arms. Appointments, taxation, military costs and overseas status are still bitterly disputed. If Hangzhou wants the Zheng title to hold, it must answer each of these claims in turn; meanwhile, Ming loyalists are still searching for men who will stand or fall with them.
nesnd_ming_court.12.d: The provinces have broken with the centre, but something has gone wrong with the government that was to receive the court. The sovereign cannot leave the capital for now, and loyalist ministers must keep writing to Huguang and Sichuan, looking for someone strong enough to protect him and rich enough to keep a court. Every extra day in Nanjing is another day at Hangzhou's mercy.
nesnd_south_offer_accord_desc: Appointments, taxation and military funding need a constitution that everyone accepts. Send our proposals to the provinces and overseas states and ask them to declare their support.
nesnd_south_retry_confrontation_desc: The last negotiations came to nothing, and those who reject the new dynasty still sit behind their own troops. Confront them again: do they recognise the court or not? Make them give a straight answer.
nesnd_south_accords.1.ming: The cabinet's envoy has arrived in [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] to seek our support for a settlement preserving the Ming dynasty. A constitution will define the powers of the centre and provinces. The Zhu sovereign will remain at the head of government, the cabinet and Six Ministries will administer under law, and provincial delegates will participate through the Assembly of Rites.\n\nTo agree is to recognise the Zhu succession and back this settlement. Our government, territory and existing laws are left untouched, and our dealings with overseas states, as subjects or as trading partners, remain as our treaties provide.
nesnd_south_accords.1.integration: The Southern Administration's envoy offers clear terms: recognise Zheng accession and place our Chinese territories under direct central administration as provinces. Their separate military and political authority will end; appointments, taxation and military funding will fall under the new dynasty's constitution and the cabinet and Six Ministries.\n\nThe centralising reform Hangzhou has pursued for years lacks only this final step. Once we agree, the question of who governs these lands and who taxes them will be settled for good. Any overseas territory we hold keeps its government and borders.
nesnd_south_accords.1.japan: The Southern Administration asks us to recognise the Zheng succession and surrender any territory we hold in Shikoku and Kyushu to direct Wu rule. Our government would retain its remaining lands.\n\nSo the Southern succession has been tied to Japan's borders. Accepting it buys a place in the new order, and the price is these lands.
nesnd_south_accords.1.overseas: The Southern Administration asks [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] to recognise the Zheng succession while retaining our government, territory and existing status. The Assembly of Rites and cabinet will settle the Southern constitution's distribution of sovereign and provincial powers. Our commerce, ports and military obligations will remain matters for separate treaties.\n\nWhat the Zheng want is support, at home and abroad.
nesnd_south_accords.20.d: For a year, the provinces and states supporting Ming have upheld their commitment to reform. The provisions debated by provincial delegates in the Assembly of Rites on appointments, land taxes and military funding now have a basis for enactment. The cabinet asks [ROOT.GetCountry.GetRuler.GetPrimaryRoleTitle] [ROOT.GetCountry.GetRuler.GetFullName] to proclaim a constitution defining the powers of the centre and provinces.\n\nSince Chen Dongyang restored provincial administrative commissions, the Southern government has coordinated civil and military affairs, but the titles of former feudal lords still sustain local influence. Disputes set aside during resistance to the North can at last be settled in the assembly. The Zhu succession is saved, and from now on the sovereign, the cabinet and the provinces each act under the constitution.
nesnd_south_accords.22.d: [ROOT.GetCountry.GetRuler.GetPrimaryRoleTitle] [ROOT.GetCountry.GetRuler.GetFullName] has proclaimed the revised constitution. Provincial delegates participate in the Assembly of Rites; the cabinet and Six Ministries conduct central government; provincial administrative commissions administer local affairs under the settlement. The Zhu house has won back room to govern from under Hangzhou's thumb, and the price is a throne bound by the constitution.\n\nSouthern Ming survives as a Confucian constitutional democracy and federation. The provinces and overseas states keep their own governments and territories, and the centre pays for the new institutions. The powers that the Southern and Western Administrations once fought over with soldiers now have a constitution both sides accept to decide them.
nesnd_south_reconciliation_reason: Chen Dongyang's reforms long ago turned the Southern provinces into something other than the military fiefs of old Northern Ming. But the bad blood between the Southern and Western Administrations will not melt away after one debate in the assembly. Now that the parties stand behind the same settlement, the centre must produce the administrative funds it promised and turn the constitution's paper powers into practice.\n\nThe overseas states are watching to see whether the court keeps its word. Only by honouring the settlement month after month can the succession dispute be brought back to a point where it can be talked out.
nesnd_south_reconciliation_stop_desc: Stop the extra administrative spending for the settlement; the effort to calm the court dispute through it ends here.
nesnd_court_followup.15.d: After the change of dynasty, the Zhu relatives remaining in [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] still need food, clothing and a roof. Supporting these princes without a throne lets them keep their dignity, and lets the old dynasty's followers see how the new one treats its predecessors. Centuries of imperial rule do not vanish with a change of name.
nesnd_court_followup.19.d: The succession dispute has dragged on for two years, and the court has still not brought the parties round to a single position. The Southern provinces and overseas states go on governing with the powers they have, and the split between Ming and Wu loyalists has not grown into a common war.\n\nBetter to let it rest here, and accept the borders, governments and treaties as they stand. No one's reforms have been carried, but at least the realm need not keep waiting for a constitution no one can agree on.
nesnd_south_holdout_front_status: Wu and the Jingnan states are still facing each other. Any state that drops out of the fighting must find its own way forward.
nesnd_south_holdouts.2.d: Envoys from [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_holdout_sender').GetName] seek northern protection. They will acknowledge the empire as overlord if only they may keep their land and their army. Take them on as subjects, and the empire has set foot in the Southern war.
nesnd_south_holdouts.refuse: The South's mess is not the empire's to clean up.
nesnd_south_holdouts.3.d: The North will not lift a finger. The envoys made the journey for nothing, and the same two roads lie before us: fight Wu again to keep our land, or, if we will not fight, submit.
nesnd_south_holdouts.4.d: The envoys have come back with the North's acceptance. Our land and army are safe, and the North is our overlord now. Life after the war is still ours to rebuild.
